author: bobyv87
text:
IF, can you please help me with this? How you deal with commissions
and still catch to the pip entries? Lets say you take an SAS trade back
to BS, and you have 1 pip SL or even 2 pips, and the space back to BS is
 2 pips. Your commission per round trip is 5.23 EUR. In this case, you
can't close half of your position at first target because you just paid
 your commission so if price retrace up to your SL, you are not in
profit, but instead in a loss. Basically, from what i see you have to
calculate to have at least 4 pips SL and 4 pips to first target to say,
ok, i can close at first target a bit over half of my position to be
still in profit if price goes against me. So how do you trade tick PA
if in tick charts you often have your first target at less than 1 pip
distance? Thank you!

author: Ifmyante
text:
I posted this elsewhere, and am copying it here, as it's important:

We have had so many great analysts, who can draw a line at every place
price will turn, yet fail to make money from their knowledge.

If we want to face the ITs and win, we must first have faced the enemy within ourselves.

Doing so teaches us which impulses to trade come from our rational,
positive self, and which come from our self destructive side.

author: einrikr
text:
Very nice one IF, and very much true I believe.

For me, going through this process feeds both wolves. Slowly but
steadily, the good one gets more of the food ;-) There are some days,
weeks even though, that the bad one has the upper hand and I feel like
I'll never get it although it all seems so obvious. Sometimes I'm in
some really nice trades and that makes me cocky and over confident,
which in turn makes me fail. That is the fight I'm currently in I guess.
 Then again, I've "just started" this all and didn't expect to be hugely
 profitable already.

All in all, most of the time, I really enjoy learning RTM and I'm sure it'll all work out for me one day.

author: HCDE

Morning everyone.

It's rare i see scales clearly, but on USDCAD i think we have a good example. I tried to represent two scales:

-Scale "X": non dotted rectangles --> See how on that scale the engulf of the high still hasn't reached it's TG

-Scale "X-1": See how they use the X-1 scale FLs to make the retrace in
order to get more long orders below before they finally get to their TG
on scale X.

First chart presents only scale X, while second one présents both scales.

Hope it helps,

Hugo
